name: GitHub
summary: GitHub supports OAuth2 with standard authorization code and device flows; creating an OAuth App is straightforward via the user settings, no review is required.

oauth_note.text: Supports web application flow (authorization code grant) and device flow; implicit grant not supported; optional expiring tokens with offline_access scope.

app_types.name: OAuth App
app_types.when_to_use: When you need a user‑centred integration that uses GitHub OAuth scopes.

app_types.name: GitHub App
app_types.when_to_use: When you prefer fine‑grained permissions, short‑lived tokens, or need to act without a user.

registration_access_claim.text: Any logged-in GitHub user can register an OAuth App from Settings → Developer settings; no organization, verification or payment needed.

prerequisites.text: A GitHub account (free tier is sufficient).

steps.title: Open developer settings
steps.detail: Log into GitHub, click your profile picture → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps.

steps.title: Create a new OAuth app
steps.detail: Click “New OAuth App”, fill in Application name, Homepage URL, and Authorization callback URL (redirect URI).

steps.title: Save client credentials
steps.detail: After creation, note the Client ID and Client Secret displayed on the app page.

steps.title: Configure scopes (optional)
steps.detail: Decide which OAuth scopes your app needs (e.g., repo, user, offline_access) and document them for users.

steps.title: Implement authorization flow
steps.detail: Build the authorization URL: https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI&scope=SCOPES&state=RANDOM. Exchange the returned code at https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token.

steps.title: Handle token expiration (optional)
steps.detail: If you request offline_access, GitHub will return an expiring access token (8 h) and a refresh token (6 months idle). Use the refresh token endpoint to obtain new tokens.

approval_claim.text: The app was usable the moment it was created. The only review-like thing on the page is an optional 'List this application in the Marketplace' button; nothing requires it.

unreviewed_limits.text: No limits shown at creation. The app page shows '0 users' and a 'Revoke all user tokens' control; no test-user cap or scope restrictions were mentioned.

approval_wait.note: Docs do not mention any review waiting period.

setup_time.note: Logged-in personal account → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → 'Register a new OAuth app'. Four fields (name, homepage URL, optional description, redirect URI) plus three checkboxes. Client ID shown immediately on 'Application created successfully'; client secret via a separate 'Generate a new client secret' button. No review, no waiting, no email.

redirect_uri_rules.text: The form allows up to 10 redirect URIs. http://localhost:8000/callback was accepted without any HTTPS warning. An optional 'Allow wildcard matching' checkbox (off by default) extends a URI to subdomains and additional paths; without it, matching is exact.

token_lifecycle.text: Expiring tokens are a per-app option: the 'Expire user access tokens' checkbox is OFF by default. The form says enabling it 'will provide a refresh_token which can be used to request an updated access token when this access token expires'. With it off, tokens do not expire.

scopes_note.text: Scopes are space‑separated in the `scope` parameter; request `offline_access` to receive refresh tokens; no incremental auth documented.

pkce_required.text: Not mentioned in the official docs; support is unclear.

blockers.fix: Log in with a GitHub account before accessing the developer portal.
Ensure the exact URL (including scheme, host, path) is registered in the app settings.
Store the client secret securely (e.g., env var, secret manager).
Use the authorization code flow; implicit grant is not supported.
Include `offline_access` scope to receive refresh token when expiring tokens are enabled.

blockers.blocker: Device flow is off by default; a CLI/agent that uses the device authorization grant gets an error until 'Enable Device Flow' is ticked.
blockers.fix: Tick 'Enable Device Flow' on the app's settings page (it can be changed after creation).

blockers.blocker: Expecting a refresh_token when 'Expire user access tokens' is off (the default).
blockers.fix: Tick 'Expire user access tokens' if your agent handles refresh; leave it off if it expects a long-lived token.

agent_can: exchange authorization code for access token
human_must: create the OAuth app in settings
accept any terms of service when creating the app
composio_note: Composio has a 'github' toolkit (https://docs.composio.dev/kb/toolkit/github). Composio's own OAuth credential guide for it: https://composio.dev/auth/github. When registering, use the redirect URI shown in your Composio auth config.

tested_notes.text: The form is at github.com/settings/applications/new; the created app lives at github.com/settings/applications/<id> with General, Optional features and Advanced tabs.
Three checkboxes on the form: 'Allow wildcard matching' (per redirect URI), 'Enable Device Flow', 'Expire user access tokens'. All three are unticked by default.
No mention anywhere of HTTPS being required, of app verification, or of scope-based review.
Corrects the generated guide: it claimed one redirect URI per app, exact match only, and (in one run) that expiring tokens are on by default.
